doc.title: Hal Galper interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, June 27, 2022

title: Over-thinking and shutting down the frontal cortex
summary: Galper describes how music bypasses the frontal lobes and reaches the limbic system, where split-second note decisions are made.

story.theme_name: Teaching jazz: schools, students and advice to the young
story.community_name: What to think while improvising: wrong notes and being in the moment

blocks.x: Well I hope I do as well. You know you made a statement on one of the videos I watched recently and I couldn’t tell if your tongue was in your cheek or not. You said, “It doesn’t take an intelligent person to be a jazz musician.”
That’s right. There’s plenty of proof of that around.
But I think also the point that you made afterwards is that over-thinking things is not helpful.

There’s a neurological pathway from the ear to the auditory section through the auditory section down to our alligator part of the brain, which is where all this stuff happens. It directly bypasses the frontal lobes. You can shut down the frontal lobes so that the music bypasses it and goes directly to the limbic system, which is where these billionth of a second decisions are made about what the next note is. You know? That’s —
